title: The bound for constructible sheaves with rational coefficients
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and a finite subextension $E\subseteq\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, with all morphisms taken over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, interpreted as the condensed coefficient rings with pulled-back ring sheaves $\Lambda_X$ and $\Lambda_Y$ [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $p\colon X\to Y$ be proper and let $d\in\mathbf Z$ bound the dimensions of its geometric fibres. Then $R^qp_*M=0$ for all $q>2d+1$ and all $M\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, where $Rp_*$ is the module-object derived pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and constructibility is [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

proof.text: If d<0, the bound makes every geometric fibre have bottom Krull dimension. For a point x of X, the pullback carrier theorem applied to x and the closed point of the algebraic closure of kappa(p(x)) gives a point z of that geometric fibre. The irreducible closed subset closure{z} contradicts bottom dimension. Thus X is empty. Every pro-etale object over X is empty; the empty-cover sheaf axiom gives zero sections, so every module and its derived image is zero. In Lean this is the direct application of Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback and Order.krullDim_eq_bot_iff, followed by the empty-cover sheaf axiom.

Assume d>=0. Finite type over k makes X Noetherian. Compare finite constant-model constructibility with intrinsic constructibility. On each stratum take an ordinary integral model; glue these using the integral-model filtration theorem. Obtain a constructible integral module N and an isomorphism E_X tensor N ≅ M. The integral constructible heart bound gives Rp_*(N[0]) in degrees <=2d+1. This already proved estimate supplies the unit's completeness, classical torsion 2d bound and Milnor extra degree; no new amplitude assumption is introduced.

Properness makes p qcqs. Apply cohomological continuity to the canonical localization-unit telescope of N[0]. Every term has zero qth pushforward cohomology for q>2d+1; hence its colimit is zero. Flat localization lets derived scalar restriction commute with pushforward, and faithful exact restriction detects zero homology. Exact extension of scalars identifies localization of N[0] with M[0].

For E to Qbar, use the scalar-basis description of restriction of ordinary extension of scalars as a copower of N. Degree-zero embedding preserves coproducts, and qcqs pushforward preserves the coproduct of these complexes with their common lower bound zero. Homology preserves these coproducts. Thus vanishing over E implies vanishing of the restricted Qbar extension. Flatness again gives the derived restriction/pushforward isomorphism, and faithful restriction detects vanishing.

For a constructible Qbar sheaf M, descend M[0] to a finite-coefficient bounded constructible complex by finite-coefficient descent. Take its degree-zero cohomology N. Exact scalar extension commutes with cohomology and identifies the extension of N with M, and N is constructible by definition. Apply the finite rational bound and the scalar-extension vanishing argument.

proof_origin.place: Localization and scalar-extension passage, using the existing integral constructible completeness/torsion/Milnor estimate and integral-model gluing; G1 Lean proof, 2026-10-24.
